stories.headline: Onsite medication injections may help people experiencing homelessness begin opioid use disorder treatment
stories.what_happened: Buprenorphine is the gold-standard medication for opioid use disorder. Starting it sublingually requires careful timing because of how it interacts with opioid receptors. If taken while opioids, such as fentanyl, are present in the body, it can set off sudden, severe withdrawal. To avoid this, patients either must stop using abruptly and wait out significant withdrawal before their first dose or introduce tiny, escalating doses over several days with initially ongoing illicit use and associated low-to-moderate withdrawal symptoms. Both approaches are especially hard for people experiencing homelessness with no stable place to live.

stories.headline: Alternative measure of insulin sensitivity may help identify risk of heart disease and stroke in people without diabetes
stories.what_happened: Lower insulin sensitivity is associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular disease. Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study collected from 2011 to 2018, researchers analyzed 6,901 adults who started out without diabetes or cardiovascular disease. They used traditional statistical models and machine-learning approaches to see whether an alternative measure of insulin sensitivity could predict their risk of developing cardiovascular disease. The alternative measure is called estimated insulin sensitivity (e-IS).
